departuresFromRN: Rejections of the ImageLoader TurboModule carry their code as a message prefix ('E_GET_SIZE_FAILURE: ...', 'E_PREFETCH_FAILURE: ...'); RN's reject(code, message) sets Error.code
repeat tiles at an integer size in points (the texture's size override), where UIKit tiles a resizable image at its point size with float geometry
an SVG is rasterized at the request's scale (size in points times the content scale), where iOS has no SVG decoder in RCTImageUtils
a res:// source is the exported project's bundle: decoded whole at the scale its file name states, like a bundled asset, never shrunk
getSize and getSizeWithHeaders read the header and believe it; the headers argument is accepted and ignored because only local sources load
prefetch and prefetchWithMetadata reject (no image cache) and queryCache answers {}
GIF is refused through onError (Godot has no GIF decoder); formats are PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, TGA and SVG
the decode shrinks with Image::resize (Lanczos) to RCTTargetSize's size; ImageIO's thumbnail rounding is assumed to be round-to-nearest and was not compared with an iOS device
the host bounds what it decodes (16,384 pixels a side, 64 Mi pixels, 128 MiB of source bytes); RN's iOS loader bounds only concurrency (4 loads, 2 decodes, 30 MB of decodes)
an Image outside the declared props fails where it renders with a host-style message for each prop the later slices implement, where RN would drop it silently on this platform
limits: Network images (http and https sources, headers, method, body and cache) fail through onError naming the later slice; they need GF-22 and a request layer for images.
No decoded-image cache, prefetch or real queryCache: every Image reads and decodes its file again.

tintColor, blurRadius, capInsets, defaultSource, loadingIndicatorSource, fadeDuration, progressiveRenderingEnabled, resizeMethod, resizeMultiplier and overlayColor fail where the Image renders; a border radius on the Image's own style fails too (the host clips rectangles only).
Animated GIF and WebP, nativeImageSource, and an Image inside Text (a failure by design, as for every Control) are not delivered.
Assets were loaded from the project directory (res://build/...) and from user://; the iOS export hook copies the manifest's files, but no exported app, desktop export or Android export ran.
The captures were taken by the macOS native renderer at content scale 2; the pixel checks sample a few points and there is no independent pixel oracle of the whole frame.
ImageIO's rounding of a thumbnail's size, UIKit's exact tiling geometry and decode memory on a device were not compared with iOS.

Hosted macOS CI has not run this slice; the oracle and the probe state values from what the host delivered or from bounds (peak in flight at most 4, peak uploads per poll 1 at a budget of one byte), never from frame pace.
Only macOS arm64 was executed; Windows, Linux, Android, iOS and Web runtimes are not covered.
GF-16 is open: only its first-slice checkpoint can close, and no whole GF, other checkpoint, dependency, weight or denominator closes.

causes.finding: addObserver answers inside the call when the request already holds a response (Completed or Failed), so onLoad or onError and onLoadEnd could reach JS before the onLoadStart that the view emitted after swapping observers

causes.source: CodeRabbit on PR #56, sdk/toolchain/asset-plugin.mjs, the assets cache
causes.finding: A pipeline reused across builds (watch rebuilds) kept the hashes and sizes of the first build and the assets the entry no longer asked for

causes.source: CodeRabbit on PR #56, sdk/toolchain/build.mjs and the asset plugin's stage commit
causes.finding: The commit placed the asset files, replaced the manifest and retired the files only the previous manifest named before the builder renamed the bundle, so the bundle still in place lost files if its own rename failed

changes.loadStart: GodotImage::resubscribe emits onLoadStart (its counter, its recorded event and the JS event) before it removes the old observer, assigns the state and adds the new observer; the removal, the assignment and the addition are as they were, and so is the status set before the emission
changes.orderRule: tests/images-oracle.mjs finds every list of events in the report by its shape (214 lists in the current report: 165 logs of JS and 49 of the views' own) and requires RN's order in each: nothing before the first loadStart, progress, one result (load or error), then loadEnd, with a loadStart allowed after a loadStart or a progress because a swapped-away request starts the next one
changes.assetsCache: the asset plugin clears its assets in onStart, so every build of a reused pipeline describes the files as they are and stages only what it asked for
changes.assetPublish: stage's commit became place (the new files go in place; it only adds or replaces a file of the same path) and finish (the manifest goes in place and the files only the previous manifest named are retired); build.mjs runs place before the bundle's rename and finish after it, and publishAssets runs both in a row

added: no event reaches JS before the loadStart of its request
no event leaves the view before the loadStart of its request
a request reports nothing after its loadEnd
oracle.limit: The order rule judges what was reported; no lane drives the path the fix is about. A response the request kept reaches a view only through addObserver of a request that completed or failed before any observer, and no flow reachable from JS puts a view on such a request: RN creates one ImageRequest per ImageState, an Image always forms its own view (ConcreteViewShadowNode::BaseTraits sets FormsView, so it is never flattened and recreated), React never recreates the view of an existing state and the host never recycles views. The probe therefore has no case that mounts an Image on a stored response, and a regression that restored the old order would pass every lane; a seam on GodotImage that replayed a state would be needed to execute it, and none was added to a class the product ships
